title: Resource Constraints in Compose
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of resource constraints in compose.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to resource constraints in compose.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Resource Constraints in Compose. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Docker Compose describes a multi-service application declaratively. It can define images/builds, networks, volumes, environment, health checks, and dependencies; startup order alone does not guarantee that a dependency is ready to accept requests. Learning resource constraints in compose helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

items.title: CPU and memory configuration
items.text: Measure the workload under a repeatable baseline and change one variable at a time. Resource options and observed enforcement can differ by platform.

items.title: Supported resource-control settings
items.text: A container port and a published host port are different values. Bind publishing deliberately, especially when a service should be reachable only from the local machine.

items.title: Local versus production enforcement
items.text: Write down preconditions, the expected healthy state, evidence to capture, and the recovery path; rehearse in a test environment before relying on the procedure.

items.title: Understanding host and runtime differences
items.text: For understanding host and runtime differences, name the relevant Docker object, setting, or operational step; predict its effect; and capture evidence from a controlled test or inspection command. Relate the result back to resource constraints in compose rather than assuming that a successful command proves the wider system is correct.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Resource Constraints in Compose
content_blocks.code:
services:
  web:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:80"
    restart: unless-stopped
content_blocks.expected_output: Compose resolves one web service and maps the container port 80 to loopback port 8080 on the host.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet as compose.yaml, then run `docker compose config` and `docker compose up -d` from that directory.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Stop and remove this lab with `docker compose down`. This is a learning example, not a complete production configuration.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
